items.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022
items.q: Harvie S. He was a young player. I just got through playing with him last night.

ctx.x: Wow. There was a period in New York when you were there, it sounded like I think I read you had some, a couple of roommates that shared your passion, Harvie S. and —

Harvie S. He was a young player. I just got through playing with him last night. He just left, right at 1:00 because he stayed over with his wife Yukimi, and they just left going back — or no I think he’s hanging with his cousin today. Anyway yeah, so I moved in with Harvie in Rego Park, Queens and he was working with Lee Konitz, Mike Abene, this guy and that. He was working all the time. So people would call him up to do a gig and say, “Hey man you need a tenor player? You need a tenor player?” So he was really…
Did your parents support your obvious bug? Your passion?
